text: He mentioned on the call the guy was french. He also mentioned that Legionaires couldn't go home.
researchNotes: A follow-up detail about Gagne, the man Larry named on the same call and said "was with me and died, he was a french foreign Legionair" (2026-09-01-phone-why-the-mountain). Filed as paraphrase: the voice is third-person throughout, which this archive treats as the giveaway whatever the source of the facts. WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE, and this is the point: the French Foreign Legion recruits foreigners by design, so a Legionnaire need not be a French national — a man could be German, Spanish, Algerian or American and still be a Legionnaire, and "the guy was french" may be reporting his unit rather than his passport. Nationality therefore remains open (ledger #18, issue #68) and no casualty search should be run on it: the wrong record set returning nothing would produce a false negative that could stand for years. The second half is the more interesting claim. "Legionaires couldn't go home" matches a real and well-documented feature of the Legion — service under an assumed identity, and men with reasons not to return to their own countries — and it is not a thing a person invents by accident. It is offered here as a lead about who Gagne was, not as a fact about him.
